title: Sword of the Eight-Headed Serpent
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep419-420_...) got the culprit right (Fujie), but several details were wrong or garbled against the transcript, corrected here: (1) its event e1 conflated two separate deceptions into one -- the pendant (o2) was planted beside the body to frame Eiko, which is unrelated to the phone-call trick that staggered Eiko's and Wanibuchi's meeting times/locations so she wouldn't witness the murder; these are modeled as separate edges (`frames`, `impersonates`/`deceives`). (2) its clue c1 has the causal logic backwards: it frames the fake registry address as something 'only someone with recent, specific local knowledge would fake,' but the transcript's actual reveal is the opposite -- Narisei City lost its name in a merger the previous year, so the address is *outdated* knowledge, something only someone who lived there years earlier (Fujie, as a Tokyo university student decades ago) would still use, unaware it no longer existed. (3) the old file gave zero resolution for the Fukuma/Eiko subplot (their mutual misunderstanding and cover-up-for-love arc, which drives most of part 2) and the Ishitobi red herring (his fear was concealing an unrelated DUI hit-and-run, not the murder) -- both are fully modeled here. (4) old file had only 1 location and 2 objects; transcript supports many more concrete scenes/props.

clues.desc: Forged registry entry lists the address 'Narisei City, Tokyo' -- a name that disappeared in a merger with Haido City the previous year; only someone who lived there years earlier, unaware it was now outdated, would still use it (Fujie lived in a Narisei City dorm as a university student decades ago).

The murder-day page of the Matsue Castle registry has an extra time column filled in for every visitor; no earlier day's page has a time column at all -- someone added that field the very morning of the murder to set up the alibi.

Every name on the murder-day registry page, not only Fujie's, is written in erasable ballpoint ink, unlike the ink used on every other day's page -- proving the whole day's page had been swapped to, not just one forged line added.
